findings.text: perf_pmu_register provides registration of a monitoring unit under a supplied name with optional fixed numeric type. It rejects missing name and out of range scope, assigns a type through an identifier allocator, optionally creates a device representation when the bus is active, allocates a per processor table of contexts with node locality and initializes embedded event context plus multiplex timer state, installs default transaction and enable operations when absent together with period and index defaults, initializes membership list and lock, then publishes the unit for identifier and list lookup.

perf_pmu_unregister removes a monitoring unit from publication. It exchanges the identifier entry to empty and unlinks the list under mutex protection, waits for sleepable and regular grace periods so in flight creation drains, restores publication and reports busy when an unmapped callback remains with live events, otherwise deletes the identifier, detaches all owned events with waiting for pending releases, then releases the unit storage.

try_module_get attempts to acquire a module reference. Absent owner counts as success. Present owner succeeds only when live and reference increment from non zero succeeds, emitting a trace on success and reporting failure otherwise.

A monitoring unit becomes observable to creation only after type assignment, per processor contexts, default operations, list and lock are fully prepared. Removal first makes creation fail through identifier exchange and list unlink before detaching, so detachment handles only fully formed events.

Identifier and list mutation during registration and removal serialize with a dedicated mutex. Per unit event membership mutation and emptiness checks serialize with a per unit spinlock. Creation holds a sleepable read side section across identifier search and list traversal with an inner regular read side section. Removal synchronizes both read side domains before reclaiming.

Detachment moves an event through revocation by exit handling, a mapping mutex ordering section so mapping creation observes state change, release of tracing program and address filter resources, single invocation of destroy callback with clearing, release of unit context reference with clearing, exclusivity teardown, module reference release and mediated accounting release, then clearing of owner pointer to turn later use into fault, followed by list removal under spinlock after context unlock.

Reclamation repeatedly obtains a referenced event from the unit list by attempting reference increment under spinlock, detaches it and drops the temporary reference, until the list is observed empty under lock, then waits on the unit address until the emptiness predicate holds, covering pending asynchronous releases.

perf_try_init_event first acquires a module reference, locks the group leader context for sibling events outside software context with nesting support, assigns the owning unit and invokes unit specific initialization, then enforces extended register capability, exclusion flag prohibition, and scope topology intersection with read scope marking. Failures run destroy cleanup and release the module reference with owner clearing.
Extended register use is defined as presence of extended mask bits in either user sampled or interrupt sampled register attribute fields.

perf_init_event preserves the original type, prefers the parent unit when present, normalizes generic hardware and cache types using upper configuration encoding with masking and fallback to raw, validates extended hardware type capability on mismatch, retries identifier lookup on missing alias, then falls back to linear list scan returning the first successful initialization while propagating errors other than missing.
Side band events for a processor are appended to a per processor list under a per list raw spinlock using read copy update list insertion, gated by a side band predicate.

Top level events update global usage counters according to attributes for mapping, build identifier, communication, namespaces, control group, task, frequency, switch, branch stack, ksymbol, tracing program and text poke, with scheduling interest aggregated into a shared scheduling counter that enables a static branch on first user.

Frequency accounting uses atomic increment with special tick dependency handling under spinlock when full tickless operation is enabled. Scheduling enable uses atomic fast path with mutex protected slow path that enables the branch and synchronizes before allowing bypass, ensuring hooks are visible before installing dependent events.

perf_event_alloc validates processor range and signal trap task requirement, selects memory node from processor, allocates a zeroed object, initializes group sibling active filter hash and unit list nodes plus child mutex wait queue interrupt work task work mapping mutex and filter lock, sets reference processor attributes group owner null marker parent namespace identifier inactive state, acquires target task reference and clock, and selects overflow handling with inheritance of program reference and backward or forward defaults.

After unit resolution allocation attaches task data when requested, rejects task or control group use on invalid context units, enforces auxiliary output pause resume capability rules with paused flag, connects control group, initializes exclusivity, allocates and optionally clones address filter ranges with generation bump, acquires callchain buffers for top level chain sampling, then applies security and mediated accounting before global accounting and list insertion with verification of sleepable read side hold.

Clock selection maps monotonic, raw monotonic, realtime, boot time and tai identifiers to respective time sources, treating only monotonic variants as safe in nonmaskable context and rejecting other choices on units lacking the no nonmaskable interrupt capability, with unknown identifiers rejected.

Permission grants access to monitoring capable callers or those passing ptrace access checks, upgrading signal trap cases to attach mode and additionally requiring kill capability in the target user namespace.

sys_perf_event_open validates flag mask, copies attributes, checks open security hook, requires kernel allowance for kernel sampling text poke or kernel callchain, requires monitoring capability for namespaces, bounds frequency and period high bit, requires kernel allowance for physical address sampling and lockdown clearance for interrupt register sampling, validates control group pid and processor combination, allocates a descriptor with close on exec handling, then holds a sleepable read side section while validating group descriptor state and output grouping options and resolving lively target task with inheritance consistency.

Monitoring unit state includes name, numeric type, scope, module owner, device pointer, per processor context table, transaction start commit cancel operations, enable disable operations, period check and index operations, event membership list with spinlock, global list node, exclusive counter, capabilities for extended registers exclusion prohibition extended hardware type nonmaskable behavior and auxiliary features, address filter count, topology mask accessor and unmapped callback.

Event state includes processor identifier, attribute copy, group leader, owning unit, on processor marker, parent, namespace, identifier, lifecycle state, attach state, capabilities, target task, clock source, overflow handler with context and optional tracing program, hardware period state, sampling flags, address filter list ranges and generation, mapping and child synchronization, reference count, wait queue and deferred work plus unit and side band list nodes.

Detachment clears the owner pointer to turn later use into fault rather than use after free and uses a mapping mutex sequence so mapping creation observes revocation. Removal refuses busy when an unmapped callback remains with live events to avoid forced removal racing close handling. Creation under removal is ordered by grace periods to avoid detaching incompletely installed events.

Registration warns once on missing name or out of range scope and rejects with invalid argument, warns on fixed type mismatch, and propagates failures for device creation, per processor table allocation, per processor object allocation and identifier publication exchange.

Open behavior defines an all flags mask limiting permitted option bits, with modifiers for close on exec, control group pid interpretation, file descriptor output and no group, and negative sentinel values selecting no specific task or processor.
Timestamping supports monotonic, monotonic raw, realtime, boot time and tai clock selections with distinct nonmaskable safety properties.
